historySource.indexText: The cornerstone was laid Oct. 13, 1792, on the site selected by George Washington and included in the L’Enfant Plan; renovations were made 1949–52. Transferred Aug. 10, 1933, to National Park Service, the legal successor of three Federal Commissioners appointed by the president under the act of July 16, 1790, who directed initial construction. Their authority developed through acts of May 1, 1802; April 29, 1816; March 3, 1849; March 2, 1867; July 1, 1898; Feb. 26, 1925; March 3, 1933; and Executive Order of June 10, 1933. Under act of Sept. 22, 1961, “the White House . . . shall be administered pursuant to the act of August 25, 1916” and supplementary and amendatory acts.
